FCCANALYSIS-SUBMIT(1) fccanalysis-submit man page FCCANALYSIS-SUBMIT(1)

NAME

fccanalysis-submit - submit FCC analysis to be run on a distributed system

SYNOPSIS

fccanalysis submit ht-condor [-h | --help] analysis-script [-- ANALYSIS ARGUMENTS]

fccanalysis submit grid analysis-script [-h | --help] [--input INPUT_PATH [INPUT_PATH ...] | --input-file-list LIST_FILE | --input-lfn-list LFN_LIST] [-o OUTPUT_FILE] [--output-dir OUTPUT_DIR] [--output-se STORAGE_ELEMENT] [--force] [--files-per-job COUNT | --n-chunks COUNT] [--sample-name NAME] [--site SITE] [--mode {wms,local}] [--ship-local-build] [--output-format {ttree,rntuple}] [-j NCPUS | --ncpus NCPUS | --n-threads NTHREADS] [--stride STRIDE] [-- ANALYSIS ARGUMENTS]

DESCRIPTION

fccanalysis submit submits the analysis defined by analysis-script to the selected backend. The supported backends are CERN HTCondor and the DIRAC-managed grid. Slurm is recognized but is not yet implemented.

The former fccanalysis submit analysis.py --where BACKEND syntax is no longer supported. Specify the backend immediately after submit, for example fccanalysis submit ht-condor analysis.py or fccanalysis submit grid analysis.py [grid options].

HTCondor

The mechanism of submission of the jobs to the HTCondor depends on the filesystem which hosts the code of the FCCAnalyses. If the code is hosted on the AFS the jobs are submitted using shared filesystem mechanism, otherwise spool mechanism is used. Custom analysis arguments must follow the -- separator.

Here is an overview where the output of the jobs can be saved depending on where the FCCAnalyses code is hosted:



  | Hosted on \ Output to | AFS | EOS |


  | --------------------- | --- | --- |


  |                   AFS |  x  |  x  |


  |                   EOS |  0  |  x  |

DIRAC grid

The grid backend first constructs the modern Analysis object from the analysis script, resolves and validates all selected inputs, and creates a deterministic plan of independent jobs. Each job receives the analysis script, its own generated input-file list, and any optional analysis helpers or local FCCAnalyses build through its input sandbox.

Grid jobs currently require a stable Key4hep release from /cvmfs/sw.hsf.org/key4hep. When using FCCAnalyses from the Key4hep stack, source the optimised release without -d.

The submission helper is started in an isolated DIRAC client environment. It reuses a valid DIRAC proxy or creates one for the configured DIRAC group. In wms mode DIRAC sends the jobs to grid worker nodes; in local mode DIRAC executes them on the submission machine for testing. Before submission, the helper lists existing output files that would be deleted and asks for confirmation. Declining cancels without submitting jobs or deleting files. Each confirmed existing output is deleted immediately before its replacement job is submitted. Deleted files are not restored if submission or execution fails. Cancellation, an empty job plan, or a submission failure produces a nonzero exit status. On partial failure, submitted job IDs and the number of jobs not attempted are reported; review them before retrying.

OPTIONS

analysis-script
Path to the analysis script.
-h, --help
Prints short help message and exits.
ANALYSIS ARGUMENTS
Command line arguments which will not be parsed by the framework and will be passed directly to the analysis script.

GRID INPUT MODES

XRootD input

This is the default grid input mode. Supply one independent input sample through --input or --input-file-list, or let the backend read Analysis.samples and resolve one per-sample input source (input-dir, input-files, or input-file-list). Script samples fall back to the global Analysis.input_dir when they have no source. Directories are listed through XRootD and contribute immediate .root files only. The backend then applies any sample fraction and divides the resulting file URLs into jobs. Workers stream these files directly over XRootD. Duplicate input paths within one sample are rejected after path normalization. Explicit paths and input-list entries retain their supplied order; files discovered within each directory are sorted by path before job grouping.

CERN /eos/experiment/..., /eos/user/..., /eos/home-<initial>/..., and /eos/project/... paths are converted to XRootD URLs before discovery. Other EOS namespaces and non-CERN storage must use an explicit URL, for example root://storage.example.org//data/events.root. URLs whose path ends in .root name files; other URLs are treated as directories. File queries are preserved. Directory discovery requires URLs without queries. HTTP(S) URLs are not supported for grid inputs.

Grid jobs receive XRootD URLs, not files from the submitting machine. Local paths are therefore rejected in XRootD input mode. This does not apply to --input-lfn-list, which uses DIRAC staging instead. Campaign discovery is not supported for grid submission.

DIRAC LFN input

Supplying --input-lfn-list selects LFN mode. The named .txt file must contain one absolute DIRAC logical file name per non-empty line. Blank lines and lines beginning with # are ignored. Duplicate LFNs within one sample are rejected. These are catalogue LFNs, not the physical paths or XRootD URLs used by a sample's input-file-list. An analysis script can instead set Analysis.input_lfn_list or a sample's input-lfn-list. Fraction-based selection is not supported for LFN samples. DIRAC stages each planned job's assigned input data into the worker directory, and the generated per-job input-file list refers to the staged filenames. By default each sample's complete LFN list is assigned to one job. A sample's n-chunks setting or the command-line grouping options can split it into multiple jobs.

GRID OPTIONS

--input INPUT_PATH [INPUT_PATH ...]
Create one independent sample from one or more remote file or directory paths. Local paths are rejected.
--input-file-list LIST_FILE
Create one independent sample from a text file containing physical remote file paths or XRootD URLs, one per line. Directory entries are not expanded.
--input-lfn-list LFN_LIST
Create one independent sample from a text file containing DIRAC LFNs, one per line. DIRAC stages the files for each job.

These input options are mutually exclusive and override input configuration in the analysis script. For both list-file options, blank lines and lines beginning with # are ignored.

-o OUTPUT_FILE, --output OUTPUT_FILE
Set the base output ROOT filename. Each planned output is given a deterministic sample and job-number suffix. The default is output.root.
--output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
Set the output directory relative to the user's DIRAC catalogue root. If omitted, each output is registered directly in that root.
--output-se STORAGE_ELEMENT
Override the storage element selected by DIRAC for output data.
--force
Automatically confirm grid submission, including deletion of existing output. Deleted files are not restored if submission or execution fails. Use with caution. Authentication prompts are not automatically answered; initialize a valid DIRAC proxy for unattended use.
--files-per-job COUNT
Derive the number of jobs from the number of input files and the requested maximum number of files per job. This overrides sample-level chunk counts. This option is mutually exclusive with --n-chunks.
--n-chunks COUNT
Request this number of jobs/output chunks for each input sample. This overrides sample-level chunk counts. The actual number of jobs cannot exceed the number of input files. This option is mutually exclusive with --files-per-job.
--sample-name NAME
Set the optional sample name passed to workers for direct CLI input. It also adds this name to each planned output filename. Script-defined samples retain their own names; this option requires a CLI input source.
--site SITE
Restrict the jobs to the named DIRAC computing site.
--mode {wms,local}
Submit through the DIRAC workload management system or execute through DIRAC on the submission machine. The default is wms.
--ship-local-build
Package and ship the active locally built FCCAnalyses installation instead of using FCCAnalyses from the selected Key4hep stack on the worker. The active stack must match the stack used to build the local installation. Workers source the recorded build setup and check their OS family, major version and architecture against that build's platform before starting it. This check does not guarantee compatible CPU instruction sets or system libraries.
--output-format {ttree,rntuple}
Set the ROOT output format used by every worker.
-j NCPUS, --ncpus NCPUS, --n-threads NTHREADS
Grid submission currently uses one CPU and one ROOT thread per job. Negative values or values greater than one are accepted with a warning and reduced to one. Zero is rejected. The command line overrides Analysis.n_threads.
--stride STRIDE
Set the event stride used by every worker. This overrides a sample-level stride.
-- ANALYSIS ARGUMENTS
Pass all following values as custom arguments to the analysis script on every worker. They are placed after the worker's own command separator and cannot change planned inputs, outputs, or supported worker options.

GRID OUTPUT

Each job registers its ROOT output below the optional OUTPUT_DIR in the user's DIRAC catalogue namespace. Without an output directory, DIRAC uses the user's catalogue root. DIRAC chooses the storage element unless --output-se is supplied. Before submission, the backend checks planned output LFNs and asks for confirmation before removing existing files. The --force option skips this confirmation.

GRID EXAMPLES

Submit analysis-defined EOS/XRootD samples to the grid:

fccanalysis submit grid analysis.py \


    --output result.root --output-dir analyses/example

Submit one remote input file directly. This creates output_0000.root by default:

fccanalysis submit grid analysis.py \


    --input root://storage.example.org//data/events.root

Create ten jobs per XRootD sample and restrict them to one DIRAC site:

fccanalysis submit grid analysis.py \


    --output result.root --output-dir analyses/example \


    --n-chunks 10 --site LCG.Example.org

Submit a list of DIRAC LFNs in groups of five files:

fccanalysis submit grid analysis.py --input-lfn-list inputs.txt \


    --output result.root --output-dir analyses/example \


    --files-per-job 5

Pass an event stride to every worker invocation:

fccanalysis submit grid analysis.py \


    --output result.root --output-dir analyses/example --stride 10
